source: Leitao, M. R. (2024). Artificial Intelligence, Humanization, and Health Beliefs. Doctoral dissertation, Georgetown University.

files.trust-by-domain.json: Study 2 (N = 106), Table 7: Doctor minus AI trust difference by medical-decision domain. Transcribed from the dissertation.
files.effects-by-study.json: Effect sizes for the chart of the humanlike AI and the doctor against the standard AI: computed from the released data for Studies 3, 4 and 5.
files.trust-by-recommender.json: Study 1 (N = 188): mean trust (0 to 10) in each of eleven recommenders with 95% confidence intervals. Computed by analysis/study1-summaries.py from public/data/study1-ratings.csv.
files.study1-tests.json: Study 1 paired tests: the seven preregistered hypotheses plus one exploratory test, computed by analysis/study1-summaries.py.
files.public/data/study1-ratings.csv: Study 1 participant-level ratings with six coarse demographic groups, de-identified (see analysis/study1-deidentify.py). Released by the author as open data.
files.study1-outcomes.json: Study 1 (N = 188): doctor and AI means with 95% confidence intervals for trust, quantitative reasoning and intuition, plus paired effect sizes. Computed by analysis/study1-summaries.py.
files.study1-test-defs.json: Definitions of the Study 1 tests and composites, shared by the Python script and the live table.
files.study1-full.json: Study 1 (N = 188): every table and model on the Study 1 in full page. Computed by analysis/study1-full-results.py from public/data/study1-ratings.csv.
files.study1-points.json: Study 1: each person's value for the dot plots, with bootstrapped intervals and smoothed shapes. Computed by analysis/study1-full-results.py.
files.public/docs/study1-preregistration.pdf: Study 1 preregistration, from the author's Word file with a reviewer's margin comment removed.
files.public/code/study1-original-analysis.Rmd: The author's original Study 1 analysis notebook, run on the raw export. Only the local file paths were replaced.
files.study2-full.json: Study 2 (N = 106): every table and model on the Study 2 in full page. Computed by analysis/study2-full-results.py from public/data/study2-ratings.csv.
files.study2-points.json: Study 2: each person's value for the dot plots, with bootstrapped intervals and smoothed shapes. Computed by analysis/study2-full-results.py.
files.public/data/study2-ratings.csv: Study 2 participant-level ratings with six coarse demographic groups (age in four bands), de-identified (see analysis/study2-deidentify.py). Released by the author as open data.
files.public/docs/study2-preregistration.pdf: Study 2 preregistration, converted from the author's Word file.
files.public/code/study2-original-analysis.Rmd: The author's original Study 2 analysis notebook, run on the raw export. Only the two local file paths were replaced.
files.public/code/study2-analysis.R: Study 2 tests and main mixed models in R, from the public file. Not yet run.
files.study3-full.json: Study 3 (N = 609): every table and model on the Study 3 in full page. Computed by analysis/study3-full-results.py from public/data/study3-ratings.csv.
files.study3-points.json: Study 3: each person's value for the dot plots, with bootstrapped intervals and smoothed shapes.
files.study4-full.json: Study 4 (N = 559): every table and model on the Study 4 in full page. Computed by analysis/study4-full-results.py from public/data/study4-ratings.csv.
files.study4-points.json: Study 4: each person's value for the dot plots, with bootstrapped intervals and smoothed shapes.
files.study5-full.json: Study 5 (N = 854): every table and model on the Study 5 in full page. Computed by analysis/study5-full-results.py from public/data/study5-ratings.csv.
files.study5-points.json: Study 5: each person's value for the dot plots, with bootstrapped intervals and smoothed shapes.
files.public/data/study{3,4,5}-ratings.csv: Participant-level ratings with coarse demographic groups (age in four bands), de-identified (see analysis/study{3,4,5}-deidentify.py, seed 2024). Released by the author as open data.
files.bayes.json: Bayes factors for Studies 2 to 5 computed from the raw data, and for Study 6 from reported statistics (analysis/bayes-followups.py).

sharing: Published summary statistics, plus the de-identified Study 1 to 5 files released by the author (public/data/, CC BY 4.0). No raw files, IDs, IP addresses, locations or timestamps, and no sensitive demographics. A demographic group is its own filter option only if at least 30 people are in it.
